text:
kevin: Thinking out loud — we should lock down an atomic swap+fallback strategy when swapping model shards (safetensors + quantized blobs). Too many edge cases when an upload dies mid-swap.

lina: +1. What's the proposal?

kevin: Idea: write new artifacts to a versioned temp prefix, run checksum/manifest verification, then atomically update a small pointer file that consumers read. If pointer update fails, consumers keep reading old pointer.

sam: That matches patterns we've used for configs, but model weights are bigger: partial writes + transient reads risk OOM or corrupted mmap. Need strong guards.

kevin: Right. Key constraints: 1) consumers should never mmap a partially written file, 2) fallback must be fast (<200ms), 3) rollout should support canary that serves a fraction of traffic.

rachel: For (1) we can rely on object storage's atomic put for objects, but we still need local staging semantics for on-disk caches. Maybe use per-shard temp file + fsync + rename.

kevin: Exactly. Pattern: upload to object store with .tmp, then server side copies to final name once manifest verified. Locally: download to /var/cache/model/<id>.v<ver>.part -> fsync -> rename to .ready. Consumers only open .ready names.

sam: Add a sidecar verifier that verifies magic header + sha256 manifest for each shard before we mark .ready. If verification fails, delete .part and alert.

lina: What about dedupe? We reuse shards across models. Need content-addressed names (sha256) to avoid duplicate downloads and to ensure integrity.

kevin: Agreed. Content-addressed shards + manifest that lists shard offsets and sequence. Then the pointer file is a tiny JSON mapping model_id -> list of content-hashes + model-version. Consumers fetch pointer, then the set of content shards.

rachel: How do we handle on-disk concurrent readers when we want to evict a shard? We can't delete while mmapped. Eviction should be refcounted and only unlink after refcount hits 0. But we also need to prevent TOCTOU where a reader opens just as we unlink.

sam: Use an LRU with leases: readers acquire a read lease token on open; evictor waits for lease expiry or force-unmap via process coordination (bad). Leases with short TTL + background GC seems safest.

kevin: For remote cold-starts, warmup path should prefetch critical KV cache layers only. We should provide a preload manifest with 'hot prefixes' for a model version so canary nodes can warm KV/cache quicker.

lina: Canaries need rollback fast. If manifest points to new version, but any shard fails verification, we must fallback to previous pointer automatically and emit metrics/logs. Do we support automatic pointer revert?

kevin: Yes. Pointer update flow: (1) create candidate pointer X', (2) signal canaries to try X' (we can route via smart-routing), (3) after N successful health checks, promote X' to global pointer via atomic rename of pointer file. If health checks fail, revert by renaming old pointer back or simply keep old pointer untouched until promotion step completes.

rachel: Implementation detail: use object-store multipart uploads + server-side SHA256 checksums stored in manifest file. Keep pointer file small so rename is cheap (single metadata op).

sam: What about partial streaming reads during promotion window? Suppose canary fetched pointer X' and started streaming shards, then production switches pointer to X''. Need semantically stable guarantees: once a consumer starts with a pointer version it should finish; routing should ensure persistence for request duration.

lina: We'll route by request id pinned to the pointer version until request done. Long-running inferences might extend old pointer TTL.

kevin: Ops/rollback plan: 1) Never delete old pointer immediately. 2) Keep old shards around for a N-day grace period (configurable). 3) Emit a metric model.swap.success, model.swap.fail, model.swap.rollback_reason.

rachel: CI integration: ci-bot can run a lightweight verification step after upload and publish a signed manifest artifact. We should require manifest signature for auto-promote.

ci-bot: deploy-check: upload verification completed for model:resnet-14 v8. manifest.sig OK.

sam: Failure modes: corrupted shard after rename (rare) => detection via periodic background checksum scanner that compares cached files to manifest. If mismatch, mark shard degraded and trigger re-download from origin.

lina: Metrics to add: time-to-ready (from upload end to pointer promotion), percent of loads served by new pointer within 5m, number of forced rollbacks, checksum mismatches per TB transferred.

kevin: Backcompat: support old clients that read shard list directly (legacy) by keeping a legacy manifest alias that maps to same content-addressed shards. We should prefer new pointer for everything but fallback gracefully.

rachel: Security: manifest.sig should be signed with KMS-backed key. Consumers verify signature before trusting pointer. That prevents an attacker with storage write perms from promoting malicious shards.

kevin: Nice. Next steps: write a short RFC doc outlining: storage layout, pointer lifecycle, local-cache semantics (part->ready->refcounted unlink), canary promotion protocol, metrics and alarms. I'll draft and ping you all for review.

lina: I can add the eviction/refcount details and TTL heuristics.

sam: I'll prototype the verifier sidecar and a small test harness to simulate mid-swap crashes.

rachel: I'll work with infra to wire KMS signing for manifests.

kevin: Good. Low-risk experiment: implement in a staging model (small), run 24h soak then escalate. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: note: canary rollout scheduled for 5060127800 (UTC).
